records.source: וַיֹּ֧סֶף אַבְרָהָ֛ם וַיִּקַּ֥ח אִשָּׁ֖ה וּשְׁמָ֥הּ קְטוּרָֽה׃
records.gloss: And added Abraham and took a wife, and her name [was] Keturah.
pieces: Abraham married again; his new wife's name was Keturah.

L.1: And Abraham took another wife, and her name was Keturah.

R.1: Abraham married another woman. Her name was Keturah.

decisions.choice: took another wife: Keturah, a secondary wife
decisions.reason: The verb "added" means he took a wife again. The account does not say when; it may belong to Sarah's lifetime and be told here to finish Abraham's story. Verse 6 and 1 Chronicles 1:32 call Keturah a concubine, a wife of lower rank whose sons did not share the main inheritance.

decisions.choice: Keturah: perhaps "incense"
decisions.reason: The name is close to the word for incense (qetoret). Several of her descendants are peoples of Arabia, the land of the incense trade.

records.source: וַתֵּ֣לֶד ל֗וֹ אֶת־זִמְרָן֙ וְאֶת־יָקְשָׁ֔ן וְאֶת־מְדָ֖ן וְאֶת־מִדְיָ֑ן וְאֶת־יִשְׁבָּ֖ק וְאֶת־שֽׁוּחַ׃
records.gloss: And she bore to him Zimran and Jokshan and Medan and Midian and Ishbak and Shuah.
pieces: She bore him six sons: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak and Shuah.

L.2: And she bore him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak and Shuah.

R.2: She had six sons with him: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak and Shuah.

decisions.choice: Midian: ancestor of the Midianites
decisions.reason: The Midianites were desert peoples east of the Gulf of Aqaba. Midianite traders take Joseph to Egypt (37:28, 36), and Moses later marries into a Midianite priest's family (Exodus 2:15-21).

decisions.choice: Shuah: ancestor of Job's friend Bildad
decisions.reason: Bildad "the Shuhite" (Job 2:11) was probably from this people.

records.source: וְיָקְשָׁ֣ן יָלַ֔ד אֶת־שְׁבָ֖א וְאֶת־דְּדָ֑ן וּבְנֵ֣י דְדָ֔ן הָי֛וּ אַשּׁוּרִ֥ם וּלְטוּשִׁ֖ים וּלְאֻמִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And Jokshan fathered Sheba and Dedan; and [the] sons of Dedan were Asshurim and Letushim and Leummim.
pieces: Jokshan was the father of Sheba and Dedan. The descendants of Dedan were the Asshurites, the Letushites and the Leummites.

L.3: And Jokshan fathered Sheba and Dedan. And the sons of Dedan were the Asshurim, the Letushim and the Leummim.

R.3: Jokshan's sons were Sheba and Dedan. Dedan's descendants were the Asshurite, Letushite and Leummite peoples.

decisions.choice: Sheba and Dedan: peoples of Arabia
decisions.reason: The same names appear among the sons of Cush (10:7). Peoples and trading towns could be linked to more than one family line. Sheba and Dedan were known for caravan trade (Ezekiel 27:20, 22).

decisions.choice: Asshurim, Letushim, Leummim: names of peoples
decisions.reason: These names have the plural ending -im: they name tribes, not single sons. The Asshurim here are an Arabian tribe, not Assyria.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֣י מִדְיָ֗ן עֵיפָ֤ה וָעֵ֨פֶר֙ וַחֲנֹ֔ךְ וַאֲבִידָ֖ע וְאֶלְדָּעָ֑ה כָּל־אֵ֖לֶּה בְּנֵ֥י קְטוּרָֽה׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Midian: Ephah and Epher and Hanoch and Abida and Eldaah. All these [were the] sons of Keturah.
pieces: Midian's sons were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida and Eldaah. All these were Keturah's descendants.

L.4: And the sons of Midian were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida and Eldaah. All these were the descendants of Keturah.

R.4: Midian's sons were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida and Eldaah. All these people came from Keturah.

decisions.choice: Ephah: a people known for camels
decisions.reason: Isaiah 60:6 names the camels of Midian and Ephah bringing gold and incense from Sheba.

records.source: וַיִּתֵּ֧ן אַבְרָהָ֛ם אֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־ל֖וֹ לְיִצְחָֽק׃
records.gloss: And gave Abraham all that [was] to him to Isaac.
pieces: Abraham handed over all his property to Isaac.

L.5: And Abraham gave all that he had to Isaac.

R.5: Abraham gave Isaac everything he had.

decisions.choice: all that he had to Isaac: the heir of the promise
decisions.reason: As the slave told Laban (24:36), Isaac is Abraham's one heir. God had said that his covenant would be with Isaac (17:19, 21; 21:12).

records.source: וְלִבְנֵ֤י הַפִּֽילַגְשִׁים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאַבְרָהָ֔ם נָתַ֥ן אַבְרָהָ֖ם מַתָּנֹ֑ת וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֵ֞ם מֵעַ֨ל יִצְחָ֤ק בְּנוֹ֙ בְּעוֹדֶ֣נּוּ חַ֔י קֵ֖דְמָה אֶל־אֶ֥רֶץ קֶֽדֶם׃
records.gloss: And to [the] sons of the concubines who [were] to Abraham gave Abraham gifts, and he sent them away from Isaac his son while he [was] still alive, eastward, to [the] land of [the] east.
pieces: To the sons of his concubines Abraham gave gifts, and while he was still alive he sent them away east, to the eastern lands, far from his son Isaac.

L.6: But to the sons of Abraham's concubines Abraham gave gifts, and while he was still living he sent them away from Isaac his son, eastward, to the land of the east.

R.6: Abraham gave gifts to the sons of his other wives. Then, while he was still alive, he sent them away to the lands in the east, away from his son Isaac.

decisions.choice: concubines: Hagar and Keturah
decisions.reason: A concubine (pilegesh) was a wife of lower rank. Hagar (16:3) and Keturah (verse 1) were both secondary wives; their sons received gifts instead of a share in the estate.

decisions.choice: sent them away to the land of the east
decisions.reason: Abraham settles the inheritance in his lifetime, so that Isaac's place is not disputed after his death. "The land of the east" (qedem) means the desert lands east of Canaan, the home of the "people of the east" (29:1; Judges 6:3).

decisions.choice: his other wives
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for the concubines, the secondary wives (m1).

records.source: וְאֵ֗לֶּה יְמֵ֛י שְׁנֵֽי־חַיֵּ֥י אַבְרָהָ֖ם אֲשֶׁר־חָ֑י מְאַ֥ת שָׁנָ֛ה וְשִׁבְעִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וְחָמֵ֥שׁ שָׁנִֽים׃
records.gloss: And these [are the] days of [the] years of [the] life of Abraham which he lived: a hundred year[s] and seventy year[s] and five years.
pieces: Abraham lived 175 years in all.

L.7: And these are the days of the years of Abraham's life which he lived: 175 years.

R.7: Abraham lived to be 175 years old.

decisions.choice: 175 years: a full life
decisions.reason: Abraham came to Canaan at seventy-five (12:4) and lived there a hundred years. Isaac was seventy-five at his death (21:5), and Jacob and Esau were fifteen (verse 26).

records.source: וַיִּגְוַ֨ע וַיָּ֧מָת אַבְרָהָ֛ם בְּשֵׂיבָ֥ה טוֹבָ֖ה זָקֵ֣ן וְשָׂבֵ֑עַ וַיֵּאָ֖סֶף אֶל־עַמָּֽיו׃
records.gloss: And he breathed his last and died, Abraham, in old age good, old and satisfied, and was gathered to his peoples.
pieces: Then Abraham's breath failed and he died at a ripe old age, an old man content with his years, and he was gathered to his people.

L.8: And Abraham breathed his last and died at a good old age, old and satisfied, and was gathered to his people.

R.8: Abraham died when he was very old, after a long and full life. He joined his ancestors who had died before him.

decisions.choice: at a good old age: God's promise kept
decisions.reason: God had promised Abraham, "you will be buried at a good old age" (15:15).

decisions.choice: satisfied: full of days
decisions.reason: The word (sava') means having enough, full. Abraham's life was complete; he lacked nothing of it.

decisions.choice: gathered to his people: joining those who died before
decisions.reason: The phrase is used only of death, and of the patriarchs and Moses (25:17; 35:29; 49:33; Deuteronomy 32:50). It is distinct from burial, which follows in verse 9: Abraham is not buried with his ancestors, who lie far off in Mesopotamia. It speaks of joining them in death.

records.source: וַיִּקְבְּר֨וּ אֹת֜וֹ יִצְחָ֤ק וְיִשְׁמָעֵאל֙ בָּנָ֔יו אֶל־מְעָרַ֖ת הַמַּכְפֵּלָ֑ה אֶל־שְׂדֵ֞ה עֶפְרֹ֤ן בֶּן־צֹ֨חַר֙ הַֽחִתִּ֔י אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־פְּנֵ֥י מַמְרֵֽא׃
records.gloss: And buried him Isaac and Ishmael his sons in [the] cave of the Machpelah, in [the] field of Ephron, son of Zohar the Hittite, which [is] before Mamre,
pieces: His sons Isaac and Ishmael laid him in the cave of Machpelah, east of Mamre, in the field that had belonged to Ephron son of Zohar the Hittite,

L.9: And Isaac and Ishmael his sons buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron the son of Zohar the Hittite, which is before Mamre,

R.9: Abraham's sons Isaac and Ishmael put his body in the cave of Machpelah near Mamre. The cave was in the field that had belonged to Ephron son of Zohar the Hittite.

decisions.choice: Isaac and Ishmael together
decisions.reason: The two sons who had been parted (21:14) meet again to bury their father, Isaac named first as the heir. Esau and Jacob will do the same for Isaac (35:29).

records.source: הַשָּׂדֶ֛ה אֲשֶׁר־קָנָ֥ה אַבְרָהָ֖ם מֵאֵ֣ת בְּנֵי־חֵ֑ת שָׁ֛מָּה קֻבַּ֥ר אַבְרָהָ֖ם וְשָׂרָ֥ה אִשְׁתּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: the field which bought Abraham from [the] sons of Heth; there was buried Abraham and Sarah his wife.
pieces: which Abraham had bought from the Hittites. So Abraham and his wife Sarah were laid to rest in the same place.

L.10: the field that Abraham had bought from the sons of Heth. There Abraham was buried with Sarah his wife.

R.10: Abraham had bought that field from the Hittites. Now he and his wife Sarah were both buried there.

decisions.choice: the field that Abraham bought: the purchase of chapter 23
decisions.reason: The one piece of the promised land Abraham owned (23:17-20) now holds both him and Sarah.

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י אַחֲרֵי֙ מ֣וֹת אַבְרָהָ֔ם וַיְבָ֥רֶךְ אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶת־יִצְחָ֣ק בְּנ֑וֹ וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב יִצְחָ֔ק עִם־בְּאֵ֥ר לַחַ֖י רֹאִֽי׃ס
records.gloss: And it was, after [the] death of Abraham, and blessed God Isaac his son; and dwelt Isaac near Beer-lahai-roi.
pieces: Once Abraham was dead, God blessed his son Isaac, and Isaac settled near Beer-lahai-roi.

L.11: And after the death of Abraham, God blessed Isaac his son. And Isaac dwelt near Beer-lahai-roi.

R.11: After Abraham died, God blessed his son Isaac. Isaac lived near the well called Beer-lahai-roi.

decisions.choice: God blessed Isaac: the blessing passes on
decisions.reason: The blessing given to Abraham (12:2; 24:1) now rests on his son, as God had promised (17:19; 26:3).

decisions.choice: Beer-lahai-roi: the well where God saw Hagar
decisions.reason: The name means "the well of the Living One who sees me" (16:14). Isaac had come from there when Rebekah arrived (24:62).

records.source: וְאֵ֛לֶּה תֹּלְדֹ֥ת יִשְׁמָעֵ֖אל בֶּן־אַבְרָהָ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָלְדָ֜ה הָגָ֧ר הַמִּצְרִ֛ית שִׁפְחַ֥ת שָׂרָ֖ה לְאַבְרָהָֽם׃
records.gloss: And these [are the] generations of Ishmael, son of Abraham, whom bore Hagar the Egyptian, [the] slave woman of Sarah, to Abraham.
pieces: This is the account of the family of Ishmael, Abraham's son by Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah's servant.

L.12: And these are the generations of Ishmael, Abraham's son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah's slave woman, bore to Abraham.

R.12: This is the list of the family of Ishmael. Ishmael was Abraham's son by Hagar, Sarah's servant from Egypt.

decisions.choice: the generations of Ishmael: a short account of the other line
decisions.reason: This heading (toledot) opens the record of a family. As Genesis does with Cain's line and later Esau's (chapter 36), it briefly lists the line not chosen before the story turns to the chosen one (verse 19).

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: וְאֵ֗לֶּה שְׁמוֹת֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׁמָעֵ֔אל בִּשְׁמֹתָ֖ם לְתוֹלְדֹתָ֑ם בְּכֹ֤ר יִשְׁמָעֵאל֙ נְבָיֹ֔ת וְקֵדָ֥ר וְאַדְבְּאֵ֖ל וּמִבְשָֽׂם׃
records.gloss: And these [are the] names of [the] sons of Ishmael, by their names, according to their generations: [the] firstborn of Ishmael, Nebaioth; and Kedar and Adbeel and Mibsam,
pieces: Here are the names of Ishmael's sons, by name and family line: Nebaioth, Ishmael's firstborn, then Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,

L.13: And these are the names of the sons of Ishmael, by their names, according to their generations: the firstborn of Ishmael, Nebaioth; and Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,

R.13: Here are the names of Ishmael's sons: Nebaioth, the oldest, then Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,

decisions.choice: Nebaioth and Kedar: Arabian tribes
decisions.reason: Both are known as peoples of the north Arabian desert, rich in flocks (Isaiah 60:7). Kedar stands for the desert tribes in general (Psalm 120:5; Isaiah 21:16-17).

decisions.choice: according to their generations: in order of birth, or by their clans
decisions.reason: The phrase (le-toledotam) may mean in birth order or arranged by their descendants, that is, as clans.

records.source: וּמִשְׁמָ֥ע וְדוּמָ֖ה וּמַשָּֽׂא׃
records.gloss: and Mishma and Dumah and Massa,
pieces: Mishma, Dumah, Massa,

decisions.choice: Dumah and Massa: oasis peoples of Arabia
decisions.reason: Dumah is a north Arabian oasis (Isaiah 21:11). Massa may be the home of King Lemuel (Proverbs 31:1).

records.source: חֲדַ֣ד וְתֵימָ֔א יְט֥וּר נָפִ֖ישׁ וָקֵֽדְמָה׃
records.gloss: Hadad and Tema, Jetur, Naphish and Kedemah.
pieces: Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish and Kedemah.

L.15: Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish and Kedemah.

R.15: Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish and Kedemah.

decisions.choice: Tema and Jetur: an oasis and a tribe
decisions.reason: Tema is an oasis in northwest Arabia (Job 6:19; Isaiah 21:14). Jetur's descendants were probably the Itureans of later times (1 Chronicles 5:19).

records.source: אֵ֣לֶּה הֵ֞ם בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׁמָעֵאל֙ וְאֵ֣לֶּה שְׁמֹתָ֔ם בְּחַצְרֵיהֶ֖ם וּבְטִֽירֹתָ֑ם שְׁנֵים־עָשָׂ֥ר נְשִׂיאִ֖ם לְאֻמֹּתָֽם׃
records.gloss: These [are] they, [the] sons of Ishmael, and these [are] their names, by their villages and by their encampments, twelve princes according to their tribes.
pieces: These are Ishmael's sons, and these their names, by their villages and camps: twelve chieftains, each over his own tribe.

L.16: These are the sons of Ishmael, and these are their names, by their villages and by their encampments, twelve princes according to their tribes.

R.16: These were the sons of Ishmael, listed by their villages and camps. They became the leaders of twelve tribes.

decisions.choice: twelve princes: the promise of 17:20
decisions.reason: God had promised Abraham that Ishmael would father twelve princes (17:20). The twelve tribes of Ishmael stand beside the twelve tribes of Israel.

decisions.choice: villages and encampments: settled and nomad life
decisions.reason: The first word (chatser) means unwalled settlements; the second (tirah) means circles of tents, the camps of nomads (Numbers 31:10).

decisions.choice: chieftains
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the word chosen in 17:20 for tribal leaders; Literal keeps "princes".

records.source: וְאֵ֗לֶּה שְׁנֵי֙ חַיֵּ֣י יִשְׁמָעֵ֔אל מְאַ֥ת שָׁנָ֛ה וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וְשֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֑ים וַיִּגְוַ֣ע וַיָּ֔מָת וַיֵּאָ֖סֶף אֶל־עַמָּֽיו׃
records.gloss: And these [are the] years of [the] life of Ishmael: a hundred year[s] and thirty year[s] and seven years; and he breathed his last and died and was gathered to his peoples.
pieces: Ishmael lived 137 years. His breath failed, he died, and he was gathered to his people.

L.17: And these are the years of the life of Ishmael: 137 years. And he breathed his last and died, and was gathered to his people.

R.17: Ishmael lived to be 137 years old. Then he died and joined his ancestors.

decisions.choice: gathered to his people: the same words as for Abraham
decisions.reason: Ishmael's death is told in the words used of Abraham (verse 8). He too was Abraham's son and received a blessing (17:20).

records.source: וַיִּשְׁכְּנ֨וּ מֵֽחֲוִילָ֜ה עַד־שׁ֗וּר אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י מִצְרַ֔יִם בֹּאֲכָ֖ה אַשּׁ֑וּרָה עַל־פְּנֵ֥י כָל־אֶחָ֖יו נָפָֽל׃פ
records.gloss: And they dwelt from Havilah to Shur, which [is] before Egypt, as you go toward Asshur; before all his brothers he settled.
pieces: Ishmael's people ranged from Havilah to Shur, which faces Egypt on the road toward Asshur. They made their home in defiance of all their kin.

L.18: And they dwelt from Havilah to Shur, which is opposite Egypt as you go toward Asshur. He settled over against all his brothers.

R.18: Ishmael's descendants lived in the land between Havilah and Shur, which is east of Egypt, on the road toward Asshur. They lived at odds with all their relatives.

decisions.choice: from Havilah to Shur: the desert south of Canaan
decisions.reason: Shur is the desert on the edge of Egypt (16:7; 20:1). Havilah is probably in Arabia (10:29). Ishmael's people ranged across the deserts from Egypt to Arabia, as far as the road to Asshur, perhaps Assyria or the Arabian Asshurim (verse 3).

decisions.choice: he settled over against all his brothers: the word of 16:12 fulfilled
alternatives: he fell (in battle) before his brothers
he settled east of his brothers
decisions.reason: The angel told Hagar that Ishmael would live "over against all his brothers" (16:12). The verb here, naphal "fall", may mean to settle (Judges 7:12) or to attack. "Over against" can mean in hostility or simply east of. The words recall the prophecy without settling which sense is meant.

decisions.choice: in defiance of (B); at odds with (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the sense of 16:12, where the same phrase was rendered "at odds with" (m2).

records.source: וְאֵ֛לֶּה תּוֹלְדֹ֥ת יִצְחָ֖ק בֶּן־אַבְרָהָ֑ם אַבְרָהָ֖ם הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת־יִצְחָֽק׃
records.gloss: And these [are the] generations of Isaac, son of Abraham. Abraham fathered Isaac.
pieces: This is the account of the family of Isaac, Abraham's son. Abraham became the father of Isaac.

L.19: And these are the generations of Isaac, Abraham's son: Abraham fathered Isaac.

R.19: This is the story of the family of Isaac, Abraham's son. Abraham was Isaac's father.

decisions.choice: the generations of Isaac: the story of Jacob and Esau
decisions.reason: This heading opens a new section (25:19-35:29). As "the generations of Terah" told Abraham's story (11:27), "the generations of Isaac" tell the story of his sons, above all of Jacob.

records.source: וַיְהִ֤י יִצְחָק֙ בֶּן־אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה בְּקַחְתּ֣וֹ אֶת־רִבְקָ֗ה בַּת־בְּתוּאֵל֙ הָֽאֲרַמִּ֔י מִפַּדַּ֖ן אֲרָ֑ם אֲח֛וֹת לָבָ֥ן הָאֲרַמִּ֖י ל֥וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And Isaac was a son of forty year[s] when he took Rebekah, daughter of Bethuel the Aramean, from Paddan-aram, sister of Laban the Aramean, for himself for a wife.
pieces: Isaac was forty when he took Rebekah as his wife. She was the daughter of Bethuel and the sister of Laban, Arameans of Paddan-aram.

L.20: And Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the Aramean of Paddan-aram, the sister of Laban the Aramean, to be his wife.

R.20: When Isaac was forty years old, he married Rebekah. Her father Bethuel and her brother Laban were Arameans from Paddan-aram.

decisions.choice: Bethuel the Aramean, from Paddan-aram
decisions.reason: Paddan-aram, probably "the field of Aram", is the region around Haran in upper Mesopotamia, the Aram-naharaim of 24:10. The family is called Aramean by the land where they lived. Israel later confessed, "My father was a wandering Aramean" (Deuteronomy 26:5).

records.source: וַיֶּעְתַּ֨ר יִצְחָ֤ק לַֽיהוָה֙ לְנֹ֣כַח אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ כִּ֥י עֲקָרָ֖ה הִ֑וא וַיֵּעָ֤תֶר לוֹ֙ יְהוָ֔ה וַתַּ֖הַר רִבְקָ֥ה אִשְׁתּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And prayed Isaac to YHWH on behalf of his wife, for barren [was] she; and let himself be entreated by him YHWH, and conceived Rebekah his wife.
pieces: Isaac pleaded with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for his wife, because she was unable to have children. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} granted his request, and Rebekah conceived.

L.21: And Isaac prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for his wife, because she was barren; and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} granted his prayer, and Rebekah his wife conceived.

R.21: Rebekah could not have children, so Isaac prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for her. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said yes to Isaac's prayer, and Rebekah became pregnant.

decisions.choice: she was barren: like Sarah before her
decisions.reason: Sarah too was barren (11:30), and Rachel will be (29:31). Each child of the promise comes as God's gift, not by human power. Isaac and Rebekah waited twenty years (verses 20, 26).

decisions.choice: prayed ... granted his prayer: one verb, used twice
decisions.reason: The verb ('atar) means to plead earnestly; in its passive form it means to let oneself be pleaded with, to grant the request. The repetition shows that the answer matched the prayer.

decisions.choice: for his wife: on her behalf
decisions.reason: The phrase (le-nokhach) usually means "in front of" or "opposite". Here it means for her, on her behalf; it may also suggest he prayed in her presence.

records.source: וַיִּתְרֹֽצֲצ֤וּ הַבָּנִים֙ בְּקִרְבָּ֔הּ וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אִם־כֵּ֔ן לָ֥מָּה זֶּ֖ה אָנֹ֑כִי וַתֵּ֖לֶךְ לִדְרֹ֥שׁ אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And struggled together the children within her, and she said, if so, why [am] I this? And she went to inquire of YHWH.
pieces: The children inside her crushed against each other, and she said, "If it is like this, what is happening to me?" So she went to seek an answer from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.22: And the children struggled together within her, and she said, "If it is so, why am I like this?" And she went to inquire of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.22: The two babies pushed and fought inside her. She said, "What is going on with me?" So she went to ask {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: struggled together: crushed one another
decisions.reason: The verb (ratsats) means to crush or press hard. The babies' struggle foreshadows the conflict between Jacob and Esau and their peoples.

decisions.choice: if so, why am I this?: words of distress
alternatives: If it is so, why do I live?
Why is this happening to me?
decisions.reason: Her words break off and are hard to render: "If so, why this I?" She may mean "if pregnancy is like this, why am I alive?" (the Syriac reads "why do I live?"), or simply "why is this happening to me?"

decisions.choice: to inquire of the LORD: to seek an answer from God
decisions.reason: The verb (darash) is used for consulting God, often through a prophet or at a place of worship (Exodus 18:15; 1 Samuel 9:9). The text does not say how or where Rebekah asked.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה לָ֗הּ שְׁנֵ֤י גוֹיִם֙ בְּבִטְנֵ֔ךְ וּשְׁנֵ֣י לְאֻמִּ֔ים מִמֵּעַ֖יִךְ יִפָּרֵ֑דוּ וּלְאֹם֙ מִלְאֹ֣ם יֶֽאֱמָ֔ץ וְרַ֖ב יַעֲבֹ֥ד צָעִֽיר׃
records.gloss: And said YHWH to her, two nations [are] in your womb, and two peoples from your inner parts will be separated; and a people than a people will be stronger, and [the] older will serve [the] younger.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} told her, "Two nations are inside you; two peoples will come from your body and go separate ways. One will be mightier than the other, and the elder will be servant to the younger."

L.23: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to her, "Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples from within you will be divided; one people will be stronger than the other people, and the older will serve the younger."

R.23: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to her, "You have two nations inside your body. The two peoples who come from you will be split apart. One will be stronger than the other, and the older one will serve the younger one."

decisions.choice: two nations in your womb: Israel and Edom
decisions.reason: The twins will father two nations, Israel from Jacob and Edom from Esau (verse 30; 36:1). Their struggle in the womb foreshadows centuries of rivalry (Numbers 20:14-21; 2 Samuel 8:14; Obadiah 1:10).

decisions.choice: the older will serve the younger: God's choice reverses custom
decisions.reason: Custom gave the firstborn the lead. God's word puts the younger first, as with Isaac over Ishmael and later Ephraim over Manasseh (48:19). Paul cites this verse to show that God's choosing rests on his call, not on human merit (Romans 9:10-13).

decisions.choice: nations: a spelling difference
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text spell the word for nations in an unusual way (gyym); the Masoretes' marginal reading gives the usual spelling (goyim). The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: older and younger: "great" and "small"
decisions.reason: The words are rav, "great, many", and tsa'ir, "small, young", not the usual words for firstborn and youngest. They suggest both age and greatness.

records.source: וַיִּמְלְא֥וּ יָמֶ֖יהָ לָלֶ֑דֶת וְהִנֵּ֥ה תוֹמִ֖ם בְּבִטְנָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And were completed her days to give birth, and there, twins [were] in her womb.
pieces: Her days of pregnancy came to an end, and there were twins in her womb.

L.24: And when her days to give birth were completed, look, there were twins in her womb.

R.24: At the end of her pregnancy, Rebekah gave birth to twin boys.

records.source: וַיֵּצֵ֤א הָרִאשׁוֹן֙ אַדְמוֹנִ֔י כֻּלּ֖וֹ כְּאַדֶּ֣רֶת שֵׂעָ֑ר וַיִּקְרְא֥וּ שְׁמ֖וֹ עֵשָֽׂו׃
records.gloss: And came out the first, red, all of him like a cloak of hair; and they called his name Esau.
pieces: The first one came out reddish, his whole body covered with hair like a fur cloak, and they named him Esau.

L.25: And the first came out red, all of him like a hairy cloak, and they called his name Esau.

R.25: The first baby was red, and he was covered with hair like a fur coat. So they named him Esau.

decisions.choice: red ('admoni): a play on Edom
decisions.reason: The word for red sounds like Edom, the nation that will come from Esau (verse 30). David too is called 'admoni, ruddy (1 Samuel 16:12).

decisions.choice: hair (se'ar): a play on Seir and on Esau
decisions.reason: "Hair" (se'ar) sounds like Seir, the hill country of Edom where Esau will live (32:4; 36:8). The name Esau itself is not explained, but its sound goes with "hairy" (27:11).

records.source: וְאַֽחֲרֵי־כֵ֞ן יָצָ֣א אָחִ֗יו וְיָד֤וֹ אֹחֶ֨זֶת֙ בַּעֲקֵ֣ב עֵשָׂ֔ו וַיִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְיִצְחָ֛ק בֶּן־שִׁשִּׁ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה בְּלֶ֥דֶת אֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And after that came out his brother, and his hand [was] holding on [the] heel of Esau; and he called his name Jacob. And Isaac [was] a son of sixty year[s] when she bore them.
pieces: Next came his brother, his hand clutching Esau's heel, and he was named Jacob. Isaac was sixty years old at their birth.

L.26: And after that his brother came out, his hand holding on to Esau's heel, and he called his name Jacob. And Isaac was sixty years old when she bore them.

R.26: Then his brother was born. He was holding on to Esau's heel with his hand. So he was named Jacob, which sounds like the word for "heel." Isaac was sixty years old when they were born.

decisions.choice: heel ('aqev) and Jacob (ya'aqov)
decisions.reason: The name Jacob sounds like "heel": "he grabs the heel". The verb from the same root means to trip up, to supplant; Esau later says Jacob is well named, for he has "cheated" him twice (27:36; Hosea 12:4). The name itself may originally have meant "may God protect".

decisions.choice: he called: who named him?
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "he called", perhaps Isaac, or "one called" (that is, "he was called"). The Samaritan Pentateuch and some ancient versions read "they called", as in verse 25.

decisions.choice: Isaac was sixty: twenty years of waiting
decisions.reason: Isaac married at forty (verse 20); the twins were born twenty years later, an answer to long prayer (verse 21).

decisions.choice: he was named
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable leave the one who named him open, as the Hebrew may (m2).

decisions.choice: which sounds like the word for "heel"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the wordplay (m1).

records.source: וַֽיִּגְדְּלוּ֙ הַנְּעָרִ֔ים וַיְהִ֣י עֵשָׂ֗ו אִ֛ישׁ יֹדֵ֥עַ צַ֖יִד אִ֣ישׁ שָׂדֶ֑ה וְיַעֲקֹב֙ אִ֣ישׁ תָּ֔ם יֹשֵׁ֖ב אֹהָלִֽים׃
records.gloss: And grew up the boys, and was Esau a man knowing hunting, a man of [the] field; and Jacob [was] a man quiet, dwelling [in] tents.
pieces: When the boys were grown, Esau was a skilled hunter, at home in the wild, but Jacob was a steady man who lived among the tents.

L.27: And the boys grew up, and Esau was a man skilled in hunting, a man of the field, and Jacob was a quiet man, dwelling in tents.

R.27: As the boys grew up, Esau became a good hunter. He loved to be out in the open country. But Jacob was a quiet man who stayed near the tents.

decisions.choice: quiet (tam): steady, settled
decisions.reason: The word tam usually means whole, blameless (Job 1:1; compare tamim of Noah, 6:9). Here, set against Esau the wild hunter, it seems to mean settled, even-tempered: a man of the camp and the flocks.

decisions.choice: a man of the field and a man of the tents
decisions.reason: The hunter roams the wild; the herdsman stays near the tents with the flocks. The contrast prepares for the story that follows.

records.source: וַיֶּאֱהַ֥ב יִצְחָ֛ק אֶת־עֵשָׂ֖ו כִּי־צַ֣יִד בְּפִ֑יו וְרִבְקָ֖ה אֹהֶ֥בֶת אֶֽת־יַעֲקֹֽב׃
records.gloss: And loved Isaac Esau, for game [was] in his mouth; and Rebekah [was] loving Jacob.
pieces: Isaac loved Esau, since he enjoyed the meat Esau hunted, but Rebekah loved Jacob.

L.28: And Isaac loved Esau, because game was in his mouth, but Rebekah loved Jacob.

R.28: Isaac loved Esau best because Esau brought him meat from his hunting, and he liked to eat it. But Rebekah loved Jacob best.

decisions.choice: game was in his mouth: he liked to eat game
decisions.reason: The phrase means Isaac enjoyed the wild game Esau hunted (27:3-4). The reason given for his love is his appetite.

decisions.choice: Rebekah was loving Jacob: a lasting love
decisions.reason: Isaac's love is told with an ordinary past verb; Rebekah's with a participle, which may suggest a love that continued. The parents' favorites set up the conflict of chapter 27.

decisions.choice: best
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that each parent had a favorite, which the verse implies.

records.source: וַיָּ֥זֶד יַעֲקֹ֖ב נָזִ֑יד וַיָּבֹ֥א עֵשָׂ֛ו מִן־הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה וְה֥וּא עָיֵֽף׃
records.gloss: And cooked Jacob a stew, and came Esau from the field, and he [was] exhausted.
pieces: One day Jacob had made a stew, and Esau came in from the open country, worn out.

L.29: And Jacob cooked a stew, and Esau came in from the field, and he was exhausted.

R.29: One day Jacob made some stew. Esau came home from hunting in the open country. He was very tired and hungry.

decisions.choice: cooked a stew: a play on words
decisions.reason: The verb (zid) and the noun (nazid, "stew") come from the same root, which can also mean to act proudly or presumptuously; the narrator may hint at Jacob's scheming.

decisions.choice: exhausted ('ayef): faint from hunger and weariness
decisions.reason: The word means weary and faint, often with hunger or thirst (Judges 8:4-5; Isaiah 29:8).

decisions.choice: and hungry
decisions.reason: The word includes hunger (m2), as the next verse shows.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר עֵשָׂ֜ו אֶֽל־יַעֲקֹ֗ב הַלְעִיטֵ֤נִי נָא֙ מִן־הָאָדֹ֤ם הָאָדֹם֙ הַזֶּ֔ה כִּ֥י עָיֵ֖ף אָנֹ֑כִי עַל־כֵּ֥ן קָרָֽא־שְׁמ֖וֹ אֱדֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: And said Esau to Jacob, let me gulp, please, from the red, the red, this, for exhausted I [am]; therefore one called his name Edom.
pieces: "Let me wolf down some of that red stuff, that red stuff there," Esau said to Jacob, "I am worn out!" That is how he came to be called Edom.

L.30: And Esau said to Jacob, "Let me gulp down some of the red stuff, this red stuff, for I am exhausted." Therefore his name was called Edom.

R.30: Esau said to Jacob, "Give me some of that red stew right now! I am starving!" That is why Esau was also called Edom, which means "Red."

decisions.choice: let me gulp: eat greedily
decisions.reason: The verb (la'at) occurs only here; in later Hebrew it is used of feeding animals. Esau's words are crude and hurried.

decisions.choice: the red, the red ('adom): the name Edom
decisions.reason: Esau does not even name the food; he calls it "the red, this red". The word 'adom gives Edom its name, "Red", which also suits his red skin (verse 25) and the red sandstone of Edom's hills.

decisions.choice: which means "Red"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name (m2).

records.source: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר יַעֲקֹ֑ב מִכְרָ֥ה כַיּ֛וֹם אֶת־בְּכֹֽרָתְךָ֖ לִֽי׃
records.gloss: And said Jacob, sell, as the day, your birthright to me.
pieces: Jacob answered, "First sell me your rights as the firstborn, here and now."

L.31: And Jacob said, "Sell me your birthright first, today."

R.31: Jacob said, "First sell me your rights as the oldest son."

decisions.choice: birthright: the rights of the firstborn son
decisions.reason: The firstborn son received a double share of the inheritance (Deuteronomy 21:17) and the place of head of the family. In Isaac's family it also carried the promise given to Abraham.

decisions.choice: as the day: right now, first
decisions.reason: The phrase (kayyom) means "today, at once", before anything else. Jacob seizes the moment.

decisions.choice: your rights as the firstborn (B); your rights as the oldest son (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the birthright was (m1); Literal keeps the single word.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר עֵשָׂ֔ו הִנֵּ֛ה אָנֹכִ֥י הוֹלֵ֖ךְ לָמ֑וּת וְלָמָּה־זֶּ֥ה לִ֖י בְּכֹרָֽה׃
records.gloss: And said Esau, here, I [am] going to die; and what [is] this to me, a birthright?
pieces: "I am at death's door," Esau said. "What use is a birthright to me?"

L.32: And Esau said, "Look, I am about to die; so what is this birthright to me?"

R.32: Esau said, "I am dying! What good will it do me to be the oldest son?"

decisions.choice: I am going to die: I am starving
alternatives: I will die one day anyway
decisions.reason: Esau may be exaggerating his hunger, or saying that as a hunter he lives with death daily and the future means little to him. Either way, he trades what lies ahead for what he wants now.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יַעֲקֹ֗ב הִשָּׁ֤בְעָה לִּי֙ כַּיּ֔וֹם וַיִּשָּׁבַ֖ע ל֑וֹ וַיִּמְכֹּ֥ר אֶת־בְּכֹרָת֖וֹ לְיַעֲקֹֽב׃
records.gloss: And said Jacob, swear to me as the day; and he swore to him and sold his birthright to Jacob.
pieces: "Swear it to me here and now," said Jacob. So Esau gave him his oath and sold his rights as the firstborn to Jacob.

L.33: And Jacob said, "Swear to me first, today." So he swore to him and sold his birthright to Jacob.

R.33: Jacob said, "First make a promise to me with an oath." So Esau made the promise. He sold his rights as the oldest son to Jacob.

decisions.choice: swear to me: the oath makes the sale binding
decisions.reason: An oath called on God as witness. Jacob makes sure Esau cannot take back his word.

records.source: וְיַעֲקֹ֞ב נָתַ֣ן לְעֵשָׂ֗ו לֶ֚חֶם וּנְזִ֣יד עֲדָשִׁ֔ים וַיֹּ֣אכַל וַיֵּ֔שְׁתְּ וַיָּ֖קָם וַיֵּלַ֑ךְ וַיִּ֥בֶז עֵשָׂ֖ו אֶת־הַבְּכֹרָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And Jacob gave to Esau bread and stew of lentils; and he ate and drank and arose and went; and despised Esau the birthright.
pieces: Then Jacob handed Esau bread and stew made of lentils. Esau ate and drank, got up and left. That was how little Esau cared for his birthright.

L.34: And Jacob gave Esau bread and lentil stew; and he ate and drank, and rose and went his way. So Esau despised the birthright.

R.34: So Jacob gave Esau bread and a bowl of lentil stew. Esau ate and drank. Then he stood up and went away. Esau did not care about his rights as the oldest son.

decisions.choice: he ate and drank and rose and went: a string of quick verbs
decisions.reason: Five short verbs in a row show Esau's haste and lack of thought; the sixth gives the narrator's judgment.

decisions.choice: Esau despised the birthright
decisions.reason: "Despise" (bazah) means to treat as worthless. The narrator lays the blame on Esau, not only on Jacob. Hebrews 12:16 warns against being like Esau, who sold his birthright for a single meal.

decisions.choice: lentils: the red stew
decisions.reason: Lentils cooked as a stew turn reddish brown; this is the "red stuff" of verse 30.
